headline: Portland schools' legislative priorities approved, covering special education funding, housing, and free meals.
summary: The list also covers student and human rights, curriculum, and construction and transportation funding. Before the vote, four partner groups described their own priorities, including limits on license plate readers and eviction prevention. The chair said the list will go to the full school board, and it can be changed later.
decisions: Approved the legislative priorities for the next session, unanimously.
discussion: Automated license plate readers: The ACLU said it will push for a broader ban on automated license plate readers, including for law enforcement, and said they are currently banned in Maine. Asked how they differ from Flock cameras, the group said traffic cameras do not share data across a broad network.

Eviction prevention funding: Project HOME asked for continued support for its eviction prevention program, which it said drew 2,000 applicants in the first three months of its September replenishment. The group said the program is funded year to year and wants a multi-year approach.

Student legislative project: Deering High School students are developing policy briefs on Title IX implementation, teacher use of AI in classrooms, and voting rights for 16- and 17-year-olds. They will present them at the Student Legislative Summit on December 17 at 5:30 at Rowe Elementary School.

Technology use guidelines: The district is writing new guidelines on technology use in classrooms and wants family input. Listening sessions are tomorrow night, 7:30 to 8:30, at King Middle School; Wednesday, November 18, 6:00 to 7:00, virtually; and Thursday, November 19, 6:00 to 7:00 p.m., at Lincoln Middle School.

decision_evidence.quote: Um but I would make a motion to um uh approve these as our legislative priorities. Is there a second? ... Okay, so that is unanimous. So, these are our priorities.

decision_titles: Legislative priorities for the next session
